report:
PASS applies only to the complete restricted A–E theorem. I independently checked the current article, the n1–n4 dependency chain, their ancillary mathematical calculations, and the relevant companion overlap. No substantial repair or additional uncertain indispensable premise is needed. Unrestricted P14 remains open; historical INCONCLUSIVE reports and candidate/publication flags remain unchanged. Reviewer verdicts, source-read flags and numerical success claims were not proof premises.

The four indispensable nonroutine foundations are recorded below, including their exact task-granted bindings. I also opened the matching primary sources. [Tosatti–Weinkove, Corollary 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.1390v2) has the required smooth positive-data existence and closed normalization. [Demailly–Păun, Theorem 2.12](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0105176v2) has precisely the compact Kähler, nef and positive-top-intersection hypotheses used for core exclusion. [Demailly, VI.8.6–8.7](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf) states the smooth Kähler ddbar lemma; the genuine global potential consequence for the current is explicitly granted separately by the task and recorded as premise 2. [Tosatti, Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.30153v2) has the stated closed-nef Morse inequality and usual-volume convention. Their imported foundations are not recursively certified here.

A and n1 establish actual minimizers and the full-test value. The base equation has smooth strictly positive target (W/H)σ/L of total mass W, and α is closed and strictly positive on the compact Kähler m-fold, m≥2. Closed Stokes fixes the source scalar; multiplying its potential by 2π gives the stipulated dd^c. Expanding Ω=Aε+Lw gives Ω^n=(nW/H)μ and γ^m=L⁻¹Aε^m+mAε^(m−1)∧w. The first cofactor term is a horizontal top-degree form, and the second has closed factors, so γ is smooth, positive and balanced. For every Gauduchon test ξ, Stokes removes dd^cφε and matrix AM–GM gives ∫θs∧ξ^m≥(nW/H)^(1/n)Dμ(ξ). The constructed γ has numerator nW and denominator (nW/H)^(m/n)H, attaining this bound. Thus Vμ(θs)=nW/H over the entire test set.

The cost numerator is WJ/H, giving C=n^(−m/n)W^(1/n)H^(−(n+1)/n)J. Differentiation under the integral is justified locally by L being uniformly positive; dH/ds=J, so C=−λ′. Holding any attaining ξ fixed gives λ(s+δ)≤λ(s)−δCξ for both signs of δ. The two limits force Cξ=C. The negative-s strict extension handles s=0. Consequently every arbitrary minimizing selection produces the same smooth scalar cost; neither a differentiable metric family nor measurability of the metric-valued selection is required.

B's endpoint passage is valid. The raw endpoint infimum E is nonnegative by semipositivity and finite by testing α+w. Monotonicity gives lim λε≥E. For each fixed test, its quotient converges to its endpoint quotient, yielding lim λε≤E after taking the infimum. The identical fixed-test argument for θt+δh proves agreement with decreasing regularization for the specified arbitrary Hermitian h. Monotone convergence gives Hε→H(0), including infinity, and hence Vμ(θt)=nW/H(0). On compact strict segments, ∫₀ʳC=λ(θ0)−λ(θr). Nonnegativity and the established finite endpoint limit prove the finite improper identity. This includes a≡0, positive-measure zero sets and arbitrarily flat zeros without an endpoint PDE.

C and n2 correctly derive all five geometric profiles. Positive density and bounded tubular Jacobians compare the p-th inverse moment with 1+∫₀ᴿρ^(d−1)/(ρ^k+ε)^p dρ. Substituting q=ρ^k gives ε^(r−p) times an integral whose tail is integrable for r<p, logarithmic for r=p, and yields a finite unregularized moment for r>p. Applying p=1,2 gives respectively the claimed cost orders ε^((1−r)/n−1), ε⁻¹log(1/ε)^(−(n+1)/n), ε^(r−2), log(1/ε), and the stated positive finite limit. Every regime is integrable. H(0)<∞ exactly when d>k. Finite disjoint components contribute positive sums, so their smallest ratio governs without cancellation. An empty zero set instead gives a positive minimum and finite positive limits.

D and n3 exclude every genuine strict potential. Compare h with α+w, and pair a purported strict current with fα^m for arbitrary smooth nonnegative base f. This smooth semipositive test is dd^c-closed by horizontal degree. Genuine quasi-psh local integrability permits distributional Stokes, eliminating dd^c u and forcing a to have a positive uniform lower bound. A bump supported near any zero contradicts that conclusion. No singular potential or current is restricted to a fiber. Conversely, a positive minimum makes θt itself strictly positive, proving the exact bigness criterion.

The projective normalization is correct. For κ=dd^c log(1+|z|²), the affine top density is (m!/π^m)(1+|z|²)^(−m−1)dLeb. Polar integration and x=|z|²/(1+|z|²) give the probability law mx^(m−1)dx and W=1. The global coefficient has a unique quadratic zero of real codimension 2m and a positive lower bound outside a small tube. Therefore H(0)=m/(m−1), Vμ(θt)=(m+1)(m−1)/m, and J(0)=m/(m−2) for m>2. For m=2, the displayed exact H and J formulas yield C/log(1/ε)→3^(−2/3)2^(−1/3); the stated finite positive limit for m>2 is also correct. The polynomial-division recurrence in n3 is valid. These are full-volume conclusions through A–B. Optional numerical and artifact-execution claims were not audited and are unnecessary corroboration.

E and n4 have the exact closed comparison. The product is compact Kähler; P=α+(a0+t)w and Q=tw are closed nef representatives. Their wedge expansions give ∫P^n=nW(a0+t) and ∫P^(n−1)Q=tW. The Morse expression is therefore nWa0, precisely the endpoint Vμ, independently of σ, including a0=0. Premise 3 applies in exactly this closed-nef cohomological setting. It supplies no cohomological application to nonconstant a.

The universal core exclusion correctly treats its decomposition as a hypothetical antecedent. Any proposed closed nef positive-intersection χ has a Kähler current by premise 1, with a genuine global potential relative to χ by premise 2. Adding the arbitrary semipositive β and undoing the smooth gauge would make θt big, contradicting D. This excludes every proposed core and smooth gauge, including nonproduct cores. The opposite gauge signs in the article and n4 are equivalent after replacing f by −f.

The ancillary differential and density calculations check. They give dθs=da∧w, d(θs^m)=m da∧α^(m−1)∧w and dd^c(θs^m)=m dd^c a∧α^(m−1)∧w. For nonconstant a, the gauge polynomial has derivative −nm∫(i/(2π))∂a∧bar∂a∧α^(m−1)<0, proving actual failure of ordinary top-integral gauge invariance. Each Gauduchon quotient remains smoothly dd^c-gauge invariant by Stokes. The normalized positive density perturbation σq=(1+q(L⁻¹−H))σ gives Hq=H+q(J−H²), with strictly positive variance for nonconstant a. Thus the specified density dependence and nonclosed differential information are retained.

Current companion overlap was retrieved directly. The [warped section](https://github.com/MingchenXia/non-kahler-pluripotential-theory/blob/main/book/author/section_warped_gauduchon_completion.tex) contains the product volume, balanced minimizers, tubular inverse-moment thresholds and smooth-test nonbigness obstruction. The [radial section](https://github.com/MingchenXia/non-kahler-pluripotential-theory/blob/main/book/author/section_radial_positive_volume_nonbig.tex) contains the scaled projective example. Its bounded radial-potential argument also checks: x≤qε≤x^((m−1)/m) gives an integrable domination and uniform genuine-potential convergence; AM–GM is used off the zero fiber, with no singular top power required there. The supplied radial normalized-test and localized-test calculations are consistent with their trace normalizations and concentration limits.

The [variational-volume chapter](https://github.com/MingchenXia/non-kahler-pluripotential-theory/blob/main/book/author/chapter_gauduchon_variational_volume.tex) contains first variation for any minimizer and nef-limit passage, and the [closed-core section](https://github.com/MingchenXia/non-kahler-pluripotential-theory/blob/main/book/author/section_nef_boundary_subtraction.tex) contains its endpoint cost identity. These matching results retain credit. A–E does not depend on accepting the companion's broader theory: its minimizers, variation and endpoint are established directly. This audit establishes no priority or unrestricted programme completion.

Harmless wording assessment: the current revisions correctly specify a on B, require a nonempty zero set for the tubular ratio, handle empty zero sets by a positive minimum, describe torsion as not identically zero, and state smooth quotient-gauge invariance accurately. No further substantial mathematical repair is required.

passages.statement: On a connected compact Kähler m-fold, m≥2, for every smooth real d-closed strictly positive (1,1)-form K and every smooth strictly positive top-degree form ρ satisfying ∫ρ=∫K^m, there is a global smooth real function φ such that K+(i/(2π))∂bar∂φ>0 and (K+(i/(2π))∂bar∂φ)^m=ρ.
passages.quote:
Smooth positive-data existence in a strict CLOSED Kahler class may be
used: for smooth closed K>0 and smooth eta>0 with equal total class
mass there is global smooth phi with K+dd^c phi>0 and
(K+dd^c phi)^m=eta.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler d-fold (M,ω), every nef real (1,1) cohomology class P with ∫_M P^d>0 contains a d-closed positive (1,1)-current T∈P satisfying T≥δω for some δ>0 (Demailly–Păun, Theorem 2.12).
passages.quote:
Demailly--Paun, arXiv:math/0105176v2, Theorem2.12 (printed12-13), states
that a nef real (1,1) class with positive top self-intersection on a compact
Kahler manifold contains a closed Kahler current.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler manifold, if χ is a smooth real d-closed (1,1)-form and T is a closed Kähler current representing [χ], then there is a genuine canonical global quasi-psh function v such that T=χ+(i/(2π))∂bar∂v.
passages.quote:
The compact Kahler
ddbar lemma yields a genuine global quasi-psh potential for any smooth
representative; rescale that potential2pi for the present dd^c convention.

passages.statement: For a compact Kähler n-fold M and nef real (1,1) cohomology classes P,Q, the usual cohomological volume, defined to be zero outside the pseudoeffective cone, satisfies vol(P−Q)≥∫_M P^n−n∫_M P^(n−1)Q (Tosatti, arXiv:2608.30153v2, Theorem 1.1).

premises: On a connected compact Kähler m-fold, m≥2, for every smooth real d-closed strictly positive (1,1)-form K and every smooth strictly positive top-degree form ρ satisfying ∫ρ=∫K^m, there is a global smooth real function φ such that K+(i/(2π))∂bar∂φ>0 and (K+(i/(2π))∂bar∂φ)^m=ρ.
On a compact Kähler d-fold (M,ω), every nef real (1,1) cohomology class P with ∫_M P^d>0 contains a d-closed positive (1,1)-current T∈P satisfying T≥δω for some δ>0 (Demailly–Păun, Theorem 2.12).

On a compact Kähler manifold, if χ is a smooth real d-closed (1,1)-form and T is a closed Kähler current representing [χ], then there is a genuine canonical global quasi-psh function v such that T=χ+(i/(2π))∂bar∂v.

For a compact Kähler n-fold M and nef real (1,1) cohomology classes P,Q, the usual cohomological volume, defined to be zero outside the pseudoeffective cone, satisfies vol(P−Q)≥∫_M P^n−n∫_M P^(n−1)Q (Tosatti, arXiv:2608.30153v2, Theorem 1.1).
